claim.pdf_says: Page 1195 (printed 1165) opens with a full-width, non-bulleted paragraph: "For example, in operating environments that include the ability to differentiate local time from Greenwich Mean Time, the returned result would be \"1995021505142781-0500\"; in operating environments that do not have that capability, the returned result would be \"199502150514278100000\"." It is a paragraph of D.31.3.2 (CURRENT-DATE function), sibling to the em-dash list, not a continuation of the list's final item.
claim.markdown_says: — Two digits indicating the number of additional minutes the reported time is ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time For example, in operating environments that include the ability to differentiate local time from Greenwich Mean Time, the returned result would be "1995021505142781-0500"; in operating environments that do not have that capability, the returned result would be "199502150514278100000".
claim.why_it_matters: The paragraph is glued onto the end of the last em-dash bullet with no sentence or paragraph break, so it reads as though the example describes only the final two-digit minutes subfield rather than the whole 21-character CURRENT-DATE result. No text is lost, but the attachment point is wrong and the run-on "...Greenwich Mean Time For example..." is not a sentence.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed against both rendered PDF pages and the markdown source; the claim survives every refutation route I tried.

(1) PDF page 1194 (printed 1164), rendered at 300 dpi: D.31.3.2 CURRENT-DATE function ends the page with a hanging-indent em-dash list. The body-text left margin on that page sits at roughly x=163 (displayed coords); the em-dash glyphs sit at roughly x=205 and the bullet text at roughly x=248, with wrapped continuation lines re-indented to x=248 (visible on the last two bullets, which wrap as "...ahead of or behind Greenwich / Mean Time" and "...ahead of or behind / Greenwich Mean Time"). The final printed line of page 1194 is the continuation "Greenwich Mean Time", at the x=248 bullet-text indent. Nothing else follows before the "1164 (C)ISO/IEC 2023" footer.

(2) PDF page 1195 (printed 1165), rendered at 300 dpi: the page opens with "For example, in operating environments that include the ability to differentiate local time from Greenwich Mean Time, the returned result would be \"1995021505142781-0500\"; in operating environments that do not have that capability, the returned result would be \"199502150514278100000\"." Its first line begins at the page's body-text left margin -- the same x as the immediately following heading "D.31.3.3 WHEN-COMPILED function" and its body paragraph "The WHEN-COMPILED function returns..." -- and all four of its lines run the full measure with no hanging indent. It is therefore typographically a sibling paragraph of the em-dash list within D.31.3.2, not a wrapped continuation of the final bullet. Had it been a bullet continuation it would have been indented to the bullet-text column, as the two preceding wrapped bullets on page 1194 demonstrably are.

(3) Markdown: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 48247 (inside the page-1194 block, which spans lines 48204-48248) reads as a single line: "— Two digits indicating the number of additional minutes the reported time is ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time For example, in operating environments that include the ability to differentiate local time from Greenwich Mean Time, the returned result would be \"1995021505142781-0500\"; in operating environments that do not have that capability, the returned result would be \"199502150514278100000\"." The claim quotes this exactly. `grep -n "For example, in operating environments"` over the whole file returns exactly this one hit, so the paragraph exists nowhere else and is not merely duplicated or relocated nearby. The rendered page-1195 markdown block (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1195/page-1195.md) begins directly at "## D.31.3.3 WHEN-COMPILED function" -- the example paragraph is absent from the page it actually prints on.

Refutation routes checked and rejected:
- "Text is present, just reflowed": the text is present, but the defect claimed is a lost paragraph boundary, not lost text. The claim explicitly concedes "No text is lost". The boundary loss is real: not a paragraph break, not even a line break, separates the bullet from the paragraph.
- "Only page-break furniture / line wrapping": no. The PDF break here is a genuine paragraph boundary that coincides with a page boundary. A pure page-break artifact would be a mid-sentence hyphenation or a sentence continuing across the fold; here the bullet ends a complete noun phrase and a new sentence starts at the body margin. The transcription collapsed a real structural boundary, not printer furniture.
- "Claim misquotes a source": no. Both quotations are verbatim. I also verified the two literal strings character by character: \"1995021505142781-0500\" = 1995021505142781 (16) + "-" (17) + 0500 (21) and \"199502150514278100000\" = 19950215 (8) + 0514 (12) + 27 (14) + 81 (16) + 0 (17) + 0000 (21). Both are 21 characters, consistent with the sentence two paragraphs earlier that CURRENT-DATE "returns a 21-character alphanumeric value", and both match between PDF and markdown exactly.
- "Does not change meaning": it does change the apparent scope of the example. Attached to the final bullet, the two example strings appear to illustrate the two-digit additional-minutes subfield; as a sibling paragraph they illustrate the entire 21-character return value. The 21-character length of both example strings is what proves the paragraph is about the whole result, so a reader who trusts the markdown structure is actively misled about the antecedent.

Severity "cosmetic" is right. Annex D is informative (explanatory/rationale material), not normative, and the two example values are transcribed correctly, so no compiler behavior can be derived wrongly from this. The damage is limited to readability and to the structure of the transcription.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed real, with one refinement to the claim's framing. The claim is accurate as far as it goes: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 48247 concatenates the final em-dash bullet of D.31.3.2 ("— Two digits indicating the number of additional minutes the reported time is ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time") and the example paragraph that opens PDF page 1195 into one unbroken line, producing the non-sentence "...Greenwich Mean Time For example, in operating environments..." and mis-attaching the two 21-character example values to the two-digit minutes subfield rather than to the whole CURRENT-DATE result. Evidence from the 300 dpi renders: on page 1194 the em-dash list uses a hanging indent (em-dash at x~205, text and wrapped continuations at x~248 in displayed coords), while on page 1195 the "For example" paragraph starts at the body-text left margin -- the same column as the following "D.31.3.3 WHEN-COMPILED function" heading and its body -- and runs the full measure with no hanging indent, so it is unambiguously a sibling paragraph of the list, exactly as claimed. The refinement: the claim describes this only as a lost paragraph break, but there is a second consequence worth recording -- because the paragraph was merged into the tail of the page-1194 block, it is also filed under the wrong page anchor. The paragraph prints wholly on page 1195 (printed 1165), yet the markdown's page-1195 block (line 48249 onward) opens directly at "## D.31.3.3 WHEN-COMPILED function" with no trace of it. So a page-1195 citation of this example resolves to the wrong page. The correct repair is to split line 48247 after "...ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time", and to move the "For example, ..." sentence to just after the `` / `## Page 1195` / `# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)` header lines, as its own paragraph preceding the D.31.3.3 heading. Severity cosmetic is correct: Annex D is informative, and both literal values ("1995021505142781-0500" and "199502150514278100000", each verified to be 21 characters) are transcribed correctly.
